expected_answer.root_cause: The nats.go client (js.go::PullSubscribe) sends a nextRequest for batches of messages on a durable pull consumer. The nats-server consumer (server/consumer.go::checkPending and nextWaiting) tracks outstanding deliveries against the stream's filestore. JetStream retention drives server/filestore.go::EraseMsg (and msgBlock.eraseMsg) on its own clock; when retention erases a block whose sequence is still in the consumer's pending map, checkPending finds the entry below state.FirstSeq and emits 'bad pending entry, sequence X out of range'. The cross-repo contract is implicit — the client assumes an acknowledged-pending sequence remains addressable until ack timeout, but the server enforces retention independently. The client's retry against nextWaiting returns the next live sequence, so the evicted range is silently dropped.
error_chain: Client calls js.go::PullSubscribe and ships a nextRequest for batch of N messages
nats-server consumer.go::nextWaiting picks up the waiting request and dispatches messages
Each delivered message is recorded in the consumer's pending map (sequence -> deadline)
JetStream retention enforcement invokes server/filestore.go::EraseMsg, which calls msgBlock.eraseMsg to truncate blocks below the MaxBytes/MaxAge floor
consumer.go::checkPending runs on its timer and compares pending sequences against the stream state
A pending sequence now falls below state.FirstSeq -> writes 'bad pending entry, sequence [X] out of range' and drops the entry
Client receives 'no messages available' on its in-flight pull (or simply does not get the message)
Client retries via PullSubscribe; server returns the next live sequence above the erased range
Downstream sink observes a gap in stream sequences with no error surfaced to the application
affected_components: nats.go JetStream client (js.go PullSubscribe / nextRequest, jsm.go AddConsumer)
nats-server consumer subsystem (server/consumer.go: checkPending, nextWaiting, pending map)
All durable pull consumers on streams with MaxBytes or MaxAge retention
Any downstream sink that relies on contiguous stream sequence delivery
expected_answer.remediation: Three layered options: (1) Server-side: have retention (filestore.go::EraseMsg) consult active consumers' pending maps and clamp/notify before erasing a block whose sequences are still pending — i.e., fail closed with an explicit error rather than letting checkPending discover the inconsistency later. (2) Protocol: extend the pull response with an explicit 'gap' header so the client can detect skipped sequences and surface a typed error to the application instead of silently advancing. (3) Client-side: in nats.go js.go, track the highest contiguous sequence delivered and emit ErrSequenceGap when the next pulled message jumps; require explicit consumer reconfiguration to acknowledge data loss.
